title_en: Tian Jiawei, Wang Guoci, Tang Wei, Gao Jing — theft case
keywords_en: criminal; theft; first instance; intermediate people's court; Guangdong Province; natural person; criminal law; determination of discontinuation of crime; determination of principal and accessory offenders; application of old and new criminal law; support for plaintiff; code theft and phone cloning; making international premium-rate calls; theft of mobile phone serial number
full_text_en:
Case of Tian Jiawei, Wang Guoci, Tang Wei, and Gao Jing for Theft

Defendant: Tian Jiawei, male, 40 years old, from Taipei City, Taiwan Province. Arrested on May 4, 1997.

Defendant: Wang Guoci, male, 34 years old, from Taipei City, Taiwan Province. Arrested on May 4, 1997.

Defendant: Tang Wei, male, 19 years old, from Beijing, unemployed. Arrested on May 4, 1997.

Defendant: Gao Jing, female, 23 years old, from Tonghua County, Jilin Province, unemployed. Arrested on May 4, 1997.

The Shenzhen Municipal People's Procuratorate, Guangdong Province, instituted a public prosecution against the defendants Tian Jiawei, Wang Guoci, Tang Wei, and Gao Jing for theft before the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court.

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court found through open trial that: In mid-January 1997, Jiang Zhengzhong (from Taipei City, Taiwan Province, at large) invited the defendants Tian Jiawei and Wang Guoci to a coffee shop in Taipei and proposed going to Shenzhen, Mainland China, to set up a site for theft of mobile phone codes and cloning to make international calls to audio-text service numbers, and then collect refunds from the international audio-text service provider. Jiang would pay Tian Jiawei and Wang Guoci NT$50,000 per month. Tian and Wang agreed. Subsequently, Jiang Zhengzhong provided funds, and Tian Jiawei purchased a code input device, a wireless air code detector, and other tools in Taiwan, which were brought to Shenzhen via Hong Kong. In late January of the same year, Tian Jiawei rented Room 19E on the 19th Floor and Room 25F on the 25th Floor, Block B, Jinxiu Mansion, in Luohu District, Shenzhen, as hideouts. On February 11 of the same year, Tian Jiawei brought his wife's cousin, defendant Tang Wei, from Beijing to Shenzhen. Wang Guoci and Jiang Zhengzhong also came to Shenzhen in February and stayed at the above-mentioned hideouts. Jiang Zhengzhong further funded the purchase in Hong Kong and Shenzhen of one computer, one printer, 18 empty 9900 model mobile phones, and related accessories as tools. Then, Jiang Zhengzhong used the wireless air code detector to intercept the electronic serial number data of domestic mobile phones within a radius of about two kilometers from Jinxiu Mansion, and then used the computer and printer to input the intercepted electronic serial numbers into the 18 empty mobile phones for debugging, thereby completing the code theft and cloning. The four persons used these mobile phones to make calls to designated international audio-text service numbers. On March 1 of the same year, Tang Wei's girlfriend, defendant Gao Jing, came to Shenzhen from Beijing. Jiang Zhengzhong hired Tang Wei and Gao Jing at a monthly salary of RMB 1,000 and taught them how to use the code input device to input codes and make unauthorized international calls to audio-text services. To avoid detection, Tian Jiawei rented another hideout at Room 220, Building 7, Huaqiao New Village, Wenjindu, on March 10. Jiang Zhengzhong and Tian Jiawei brought the intercepted mobile phone electronic serial number data to the new hideout. Wang Guoci, Tang Wei, and Gao Jing used the code input device there to input the electronic serial number data into the 18 9900 model mobile phones and continuously made unauthorized international calls to audio-text services in three shifts per day.

On March 20 of the same year, the public security organs received a report from the public and arrested the defendants Tang Wei and Gao Jing at Room 220, Building 7, Huaqiao New Village. Subsequently, Tang Wei led the public security officers to Jinxiu Mansion to arrest the defendants Tian Jiawei and Wang Guoci. The seized items included one wireless air code detector, one code input device, one computer, one printer, 14 computer disks, 18 Motorola 9900 model mobile phones, 5 AC voltage stabilizers, 28 vehicle batteries (empty shells), 28 cigarette lighters, 29 plugs, 3 chargers, one notebook recording unauthorized international calls to audio-text numbers, data for 726 mobile phone serial numbers, and some personal belongings of Tian Jiawei and Wang Guoci. Upon interrogation, all four defendants confessed to the crime of being hired by Jiang Zhengzhong to make unauthorized international calls to audio-text numbers. Testing revealed that each of the 18 seized mobile phones contained one stolen mobile phone serial number. Among these, 11 electronic serial numbers had already been used to make calls to international audio-text services and incurred charges. Among the 726 electronic serial numbers seized, 631 belonged to Shenzhen subscribers. Among those, 320 Shenzhen subscribers had their numbers used to make unauthorized calls to international audio-text services and incurred charges. The calculation showed that the call charges for the 331 Shenzhen subscribers whose numbers were used to make unauthorized international calls to audio-text services amounted to RMB 580,649.38. According to the Shenzhen Telecommunications Bureau's regulations, the network access fees for the 320 Shenzhen subscribers whose numbers were stolen and cloned and for the 18 mobile phones totaled RMB 1,155,960.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the scene inspection record, seized tools, material evidence, and documentary evidence. All defendants also confessed to the crimes.

During the trial, the defendant Wang Guoci and his defense counsel argued: Wang Guoci had clearly informed Jiang Zhengzhong on March 14 that he was resigning and would no longer make unauthorized calls to international audio-text services, and had already asked a friend in Hong Kong to purchase a plane ticket back to Taiwan for March 21. This, they argued, constituted a discontinuation of the crime and warranted a mitigated punishment. The defense counsel for defendant Tang Wei argued that Tang Wei had assisted the public security officers in apprehending his co-defendants, constituting meritorious performance, and requested a lighter or mitigated punishment.

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court held:

The Supreme People's Court's Reply No. Fa Fu [1995] No. 6, dated September 13, 1995, on How to Characterize Cases of Illegally Copying Mobile Phone Code Numbers, provides that the act of illegally copying stolen mobile phone code numbers shall be severely punished as theft under Article 152 of the 1979 Criminal Law, with the amount of theft calculated based on the mobile phone network access fee stipulated by the local postal and telecommunications authorities. Those who knowingly use illegally copied mobile phones and cause losses to others shall also be held criminally liable for theft, with the amount of theft calculated based on the actual losses of the legitimate mobile phone users. The Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Severely Punishing Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy amended the statutory punishment under Article 152 of the 1979 Criminal Law to: "If the circumstances are especially serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death, and may also be sentenced to confiscation of property." Article 265 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, effective as of October 1, 1997, provides that anyone who, for the purpose of profit, steals and connects to another person's communication line, copies another person's telecommunication code number, or knowingly uses telecommunication equipment or facilities that have been stolen and connected or copied shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 264 on theft. The statutory punishment under Article 264 is: "If the amount is especially huge or there are other especially serious circumstances, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years or life imprisonment, and shall also be fined or have property confiscated."

The defendants Tian Jiawei, Wang Guoci, Tang Wei, and Gao Jing, defying national law, stole and illegally copied 338 mobile phone numbers of others, causing losses to the local postal and telecommunications authorities in network access fees of RMB 1,155,960; they then used the illegally copied mobile phones to make unauthorized calls to international audio-text services, causing call charge losses of RMB 580,649.38 to legitimate mobile phone users. The amount of theft is especially huge. Their conduct violates the provisions of Article 152 of the 1979 Criminal Law and Articles 265 and 264 of the new Criminal Law, and all constitute the crime of theft. Since the new Criminal Law imposes lighter punishments than the 1979 Criminal Law, in accordance with Article 12 of the new Criminal Law, this case shall be punished under the new Criminal Law.

In accordance with Article 25 of the Criminal Law, the defendants Tian Jiawei, Wang Guoci, Tang Wei, and Gao Jing jointly committed intentional crimes. In the joint crime, Tian Jiawei and Wang Guoci played major roles and are principals. In accordance with Article 26, paragraph 3 of the Criminal Law, they shall be punished for all the crimes in which they participated. The criminal acts of code theft and cloning committed by Tian Jiawei and Wang Guoci not only infringed on state property and the lawful property rights of citizens but also endangered national security to a certain extent. In accordance with Article 56 of the Criminal Law, they shall also be sentenced to deprivation of political rights. The tools of crime transferred with the case and some personal belongings of Tian Jiawei and Wang Guoci shall be confiscated and turned over to the state treasury in accordance with Article 64 of the Criminal Law. Regarding the defense argument by Wang Guoci and his counsel that Wang Guoci had discontinued the crime, upon investigation, since Jiang Zhengzhong is at large, the claim by Wang Guoci that he clearly informed Jiang Zhengzhong of his resignation on March 14 cannot be verified. Even if it were verified that Wang Guoci asked someone to purchase a return ticket and that Wang Guoci proposed resignation to Jiang Zhengzhong, Wang Guoci was still engaged in the criminal activity of making unauthorized calls to international audio-text services from after March 14 until his arrest. Therefore, he does not have the circumstance of "voluntarily abandoning the crime or voluntarily and effectively preventing the occurrence of the criminal result during the course of the crime" and does not meet the provisions of Article 24 of the Criminal Law. The defense argument regarding discontinuation of the crime is not accepted. The defendants Tang Wei and Gao Jing played secondary roles in the joint crime and are accessories. After arrest, they both frankly confessed to the criminal facts. Tang Wei also assisted the investigators in apprehending his co-defendants, constituting meritorious performance. In accordance with Articles 27 and 68 of the Criminal Law, their punishment shall be mitigated.

Accordingly, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court made the following judgment:

1. Defendant Tian Jiawei is convicted of theft and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 11 years, with deprivation of political rights for 3 years.
2. Defendant Wang Guoci is convicted of theft and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 10 years, with deprivation of political rights for 3 years.
3. Defendant Tang Wei is convicted of theft and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 1 year.
4. Defendant Gao Jing is convicted of theft and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 1 year.
5. The tools of crime transferred with the case and the personal belongings of defendants Tian Jiawei and Wang Guoci are all confiscated and turned over to the state treasury in accordance with the law.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, none of the defendants Tian Jiawei, Wang Guoci, Tang Wei, and Gao Jing appealed. The judgment has become legally effective.
